Okay, Brianna. On y va. (a treatise on freedom of speech and brianna wu's unhinged accusations)

There's a canard that we don't understand the right to free speech - how its just a limitation placed on government action. It doesn't obligate Reddit, Kotaku, or whoever to give us space on their platform. It's not that we fail to understand this distinction - we reject it. Free speech is not just a legal right, but a moral right, and an ideal about how society should function. People should debate challenging ideas rather than hiding from them. The recent censorship on Reddit is couched in the rhetoric of "safety", echoing the campus usage of the term, where to be unsafe means to be criticized. This stands in proper Orwellian style in total contrast to being actually physically threatened.

That is my favorite part of the post; I was going to repost it myself. I am so, so tired of always seeing SJWs and censor / ban apologists say that the First Amendment doesn't apply and that "You have the freedom to say what you want, but not to escape the consequences of what you say". Isn't that also true of government restrictions on speech? The blogger in Saudi Arabia who was sentenced to 1000 lashes for criticizing Islam was able to say what he wanted, but is now suffering the consequences. And when you can get doxxed and lose your job merely for expressing an opinion, you have no freedom of speech.

"Free speech only applies to government."

The first and last refuge of the person who despises free speech. If you really respected it, you'd practise it without being required to, simple as it gets.
Voaters of FatPeopleHate: What motivates you to hate fat people?

Let's see; should we start with the drain they put on Healthcare and the economy? Or should we talk about how selfish and inconsiderate they are? Should we talk about how their size intrudes on other people? Should we talk about their poor hygiene? You tell me, where should we start?

I don't hate fat people. Living in America, you can't help but have a few fat friends.

What I hate is the Health-At-Every-Size movement. No, you can't be 100lbs overweight and still be healthy. You're killing yourself, and by promoting that idea you're killing others.

What I hate is the hypocrisy. I hate that people can openly tell a thin person to "eat a sandwich," but god forbid I tell an obese person to walk a mile or eat a salad.

What I hate is the laziness and lack of drive. Being fit is by no means an easy accomplishment. There are plenty of days where I don't feel like exercising, but I do it anyways. There are plenty of times where I want to eat something that I know is bad for me, but I choose to not eat it, or I make up for it by running an extra mile.

I hate that people are giving up on health. Instead of dieting and exercising, people are choosing to accept themselves as fat and push the idea on others. It seems that instead of doing something about the rising numbers of obese people, society is choosing to accept that it will always be this way and that there's nothing that can be done. We can do something! We can exercise, we can eat less, we can change!

I don't hate fat people, I hate what they have done and are doing to society.
Thanks for the good-quality reply. I really wasn't expecting many of those here. It's good to know there are some rational-minded people in the shitlord ranks. Once again, thanks!

I'm not at all involved with FPH. I just don't understand it.

To me, hating something means actively being mad about something, putting effort into it... if I don't like something, I just stay away from it.

My hatred is focused on the HAES movement and fat culture in general, not the actual people. My reasons for hating fat acceptance isn't economical impacts or regular interactions, it's how fat acceptance is actively harming the people I love.

My grandfather was put in a nursing home in his early 50's, due to medical problems exacerbated by his obese lifestyle. He lost motor control over his legs and his right arm. He lived there for around 12 years, wearing diapers, and barely being able to feed himself. The inability to walk made the problem worse, and he continued to gain weight. My grandmother was also fat, and had many health problems associated with obesity. She died when I was in my late teens, and my grandfather in the nursing home died later that same year, both around the age of 60.

This last year, my dad, who weighed ~450 lbs, had a massive heart attack. He had 95-98% blockage in his major arteries, and his body actually grew it's own bypasses to handle the strain. It is only by the skilled hands of several talented surgeons that he lived, but only barely. He was in an induced coma for a week, and was in the hospital for almost a month. He has since lost around 150 lbs. Both of my uncles are severely obese. It's only a matter of time before they have their own versions of this story, as they did not change their lifestyle even after seeing what it did to my dad.

Now I see my mom and brother going down the same road. My mother jumps from fad diet to fad diet, but she critically fails at portion control or exercise. By brother is 18 this year, and is hitting the 450 mark my dad had when he had his heart attack. He doesn't care about his weight and won't even acknowledge that the problem exists. If he doesn't turn his life around, I don't see him reaching 30. My best friend and his wife are both obese. Every time I see them, they just look worse and worse.

So the reason I hate fat people is because I know the personal pain their lifestyle has on the the people that love them.
It's hate. You're not going to get many people who will rationally explain it because it's not entirely, or sometimes even at all, rational.
